findings.reason: Confirmed at v3 §1(d), p.5 ('h±_M(k) = |F±_k(Z)| … otherwise h_M(k) ≤ h±_M(k)'). The same sentence is in v1 (p.4) and v2 (p.5). The smallest counterexample is k = 5: (0, 1, 2) ∈ V_5(ℤ), so h_M(5) ≥ 1, while F⁺_5(ℤ) = ∅ because u₁² + u₂² + u₃² + u₁u₂u₃ ≥ 54 on u_j ≥ 3 (§8, p.22: 'the smallest value of the polynomial is 54'). So h⁺_M(5) = 0. The general argument also holds. In §4.1 (4.1), genericity is used only to make the brackets 2(k − 5) + (x_i² − 4)(x_j² − 4) positive, and they are positive whenever k ≥ 5 and |x_i|, |x_j| ≥ 3. The up-tree of an F⁺-root is then closed under Γ, so the F⁺-roots stay pairwise inequivalent, and no orbit through a point with a coordinate in {0, ±1, ±2} contains one of them. I reproduced the counts independently, enumerating every F⁺ value up to 100,800: 7,105 exceptional k ≥ 5 have F⁺_k(ℤ) = ∅, the last being 100,792, and k = 58 is among them; the generic Hasse-failure count is 7,630. One evidence slip: 7,630 is not an entry of Table 4, which starts at K = 6,552,000. It matches Table 3, where the 12.97620% at K = 100,800 is 7,630 of the 58,800 admissible k. The fix is right as stated: correct item 5 and add E21 (affects nothing, since (1.6) and §7 count h^±).

Confirmed as a cross-referencing gap, low. PAPER-GAMBURD-MAGEE-RONAN-19/1 is x₁² + … + x_n² = a·x₁⋯x_n + k with the moves m_j. Its n = 3, a = 1 case is exactly V_k and the Vieta involutions of items 3–4. GMR route 1 goes to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.4, and its review accepted it. CA.4 has the nodes markoff-root-generation and markoff-tree. One step of the evidence is misworded. It is not true that 'mod 3 the sum x₁² + x₂² + x₃² can vanish only when every x_j ≡ 0', since 1 + 1 + 1 ≡ 0. The correct argument goes through the product. If every x_j ≢ 0 (mod 3), the squares sum to 0 while x₁x₂x₃ ≢ 0. If some x_j ≡ 0, the product vanishes, so the squares force every x_j ≡ 0. So 3 | x, and x = 3y gives y₁² + y₂² + y₃² = 3y₁y₂y₃, as the finding says. The fix stands.

Confirmed. (a) v3 §10, p.34, says 'By the arguments in Sec. 7, … AHF(K) ≫ K^{1/2−ε}'. v3 §7 is 'The average of h±: counting lattice points', and the Hasse failures are built in §8. v1 reads 'Sec. 6', which was then its counting section (its §7 was 'Failures of the Hasse Principle'), so the slip predates the renumbering. (b) v3 §10, p.34, says 'The number of admissible k's (see Sec. 3)'. §3 (Bhargava cubes) never mentions admissibility, and v1 and v2 print the same sentence. (c) Proposition 8.1(ii) requires every prime factor of ν ≡ ±1 (mod 8), so 3 ∤ ν and only ν ≡ ±4 (mod 9) can occur. The instances below 50 are ν = 23, 31, 41, 49. k = 4 + 2·23² = 1062 is admissible, not exceptional, and has F⁺_{1062}(ℤ) = ∅ in my enumeration, so it is a Hasse failure.
